speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for sharing that. To better understand your condition, can you tell me how long these episodes have been occurring and if there is anything that seems to trigger or worsen them?

speaker: Patient
text: 59-year-old female. The patient reports a 1-month history of episodic cough and shortness of breath. The cough is nonproductive and worsens when climbing stairs and at night. She experienced fever, sore throat, and nasal congestion 8 weeks ago.

speaker: Doctor
text: Did the fever, sore throat, and nasal congestion resolve completely after a few weeks, or have you had lingering symptoms since then? REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count, C-Reactive_Protein. REQUEST IMAGES: Chest_XRay.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is surprising given your recent upper respiratory infection. Has the shortness of breath ever occurred at rest, or does it strictly happen during exertion? Also, have you noticed any wheezing or chest tightness during these episodes?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Episodic cough and shortness of breath. I also have Cough worsens with exertion and at night, History of recent upper respiratory tract infection symptoms such as fever, sore throat, and nasal congestion.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Post-infectious Cough Variant Asthma. The combination of recent URI, nocturnal worsening, exertional dyspnea, and normal inflammatory markers strongly suggests airway hyperreactivity triggered by the initial infection, even in the absence of current wheezing or tightness.
